title: intake-policy-adapter-and-prose-release-composer
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: We need a lighter-weight intake policy layer that captures onboarding policy decisions (privacy level, allowed telemetry, retention buckets, and visibility) at ingest-time and produces a compact, human-friendly attachment used by downstream changelog tooling. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) an Intake Policy Adapter that normalizes onboarding metadata from multiple sources (onboard CLI, UI, S3 manifests) into a canonical policy object; 2) a Prose Release Composer that synthesizes short, human-readable release notes from the canonical policy and profile delta, intended for product-facing changelogs and Linear ticket descriptions. Goals: reduce manual work for release authors, make release notes more consistent, and ensure onboarding policies are discoverable in audit trails. What this changes: - intake/policy/adapter.py: new adapter that validates and normalizes policy fields with a small rule engine and schema hints - intake/schemas/policy_schema.yaml: canonical schema + migration helper - tools/release/composer.py: Prose composer that maps policy diffs and profile highlights to 1-2 paragraph release blurbs - cli/onboard: integration hook to emit canonical-policy.json to the model bundle - docs/onboarding/release-notes.md: guidance and templates for generated prose - tests/*: unit and integration tests for normalization and composer outputs Compatibility: adapter accepts legacy manifest keys and preserves provenance so existing ingesters continue to work. The prose composer is optional and gated behind a feature flag (RELEASE_COMPOSER=true) to allow gradual rollout. Checklist: - [x] schema and adapter implementation - [x] feature-flag gating in CLI hook - [x] unit tests for normalization and composer heuristics - [x] e2e test that generates a sample release blurb from a real onboarding bundle - [x] docs update with templates and examples Migration notes: existing model bundles will be scanned by the intake worker and field-mapped; where mappings are ambiguous the adapter emits a review-needed marker and creates a Linear ticket (ENG-4521) for curation. Backwards compatibility hooks are included for the most common legacy fields: owner_email, telemetry_level -> privacy.level, sample_size -> profile.sampled_requests. Related: builds on the onboarding metadata stabilization work and complements the release automation prototype (see ENG-3120).
commits_summary: 6 commits: initial adapter and schema; composer draft; CLI hook; tests and fixtures; docs; polish and lints. Key commits: 1) add canonical policy schema and migration helper 2) implement adapter normalization and rule engine 3) add prose composer and mapping rules 4) wire CLI to emit canonical-policy.json 5) add unit + e2e tests 6) docs and template examples
review_comments: Jonah Reed: Nice direction — two requests: 1) make the adapter deterministic for tie-breaking ambiguous sources; 2) add a short timeout in the CLI hook so onboarding doesn't block if a remote manifest is slow.

Maya Patel (author): Addressed both. Adapter now prefers explicit user-supplied fields over inferred ones and emits a deterministic ordering; CLI hook now falls back to cached manifest after 3s and records 'manifest_timeout' in provenance.
Clara Nguyen: Composer output looks good. Please ensure the generated blurb never contains raw PII; add a sanitize step for owner fields.
Maya Patel (author): Added sanitize step and tests; composer strips emails and replaces with 'team <redacted>'.
Diego Morales: Approving pending CI. Suggests adding a small sample to the docs showing before/after release blurb for a typical privacy-level change.
Maya Patel (author): Added before/after example to docs per Diego's suggestion.
ci_logs_summary: All unit tests passed; integration job 'composer-e2e' passed with sample bundle; linter had 2 minor style warnings that were fixed in final commit; CI flake in windows runner triggered a single rerun of tests but overall status green.
release_notes: - Introduces an Intake Policy Adapter to canonicalize onboarding metadata (privacy, telemetry, retention, visibility). - Adds a Prose Release Composer that generates short human-readable release notes from policy and profile deltas. - CLI hookup to emit canonical-policy.json as part of model bundle. - Docs: onboarding release-note templates and examples. Notes: Composer behind feature flag; migration emits review-needed markers for ambiguous legacy fields.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Enable RELEASE_COMPOSER for internal dogfood org next week and gather feedback. 2) Add an automated job to scan model bundles for 'review-needed' markers and create Linear tickets. 3) Observe composer output for first 100 model releases and tune mapping heuristics.
notes_for_release_manager: Generated prose is intended for human review before publish; do not auto-post to public changelog until composer has been dogfooded and we reach less than 5% manual edits across 100 samples.
human_review_examples: Example 1 (privacy tightening): 'Updated model onboarding: privacy level set to "protected" for this release, telemetry collection reduced to aggregated usage counts only. No user-identifying fields are retained.' Example 2 (profile highlight): 'Performance profile updated: typical 512-token throughput improved by 18% after quantized variant selection. Recommended to pin variant v2.1 for high-throughput routes.'
notes: This PR aims to reduce churn in release drafting while preserving legal/audit constraints. Known limitations: composer currently focuses on the most-common policy changes (privacy, telemetry, sample size, visibility) and is not yet tuned for multilingual or compliance-region-specific phrasing.
security_considerations: composer strips obvious PII from generated text; adapter records provenance and review-needed flags when mappings are ambiguous. Security reviewed by security lead in PR thread.
audit_and_provenance: Every canonical-policy.json includes a provenance header (source_paths, resolved_at, mapping_trace) and a signature field to facilitate audit and rollback.
